```{=html}
<h2 class="rpc-term-heading">Spring 2026</h2>

<div class="rpc-course-grid">

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 214</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Data Analysis and Machine Learning for Real-World Decision Making</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Applied machine learning for real-world decision-making. Model evaluation under uncertainty, causal inference methods, and practical deployment of ML systems for high-impact decisions.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Python</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Applied ML</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Causal Inference</span>
    </div>
    <a class="rpc-course-link" href="posts/stat214-lab1/index.html">PECARN Traumatic Brain Injury Analysis →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 230A</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Linear Models</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Regression theory from OLS and the Gauss-Markov theorem through GLMs and generalized estimating equations. Heteroskedasticity, cluster-robust inference, model selection, shrinkage methods, and extensions to categorical and count outcomes.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Python</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Regression</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">GLMs</span>
    </div>
    <a class="rpc-course-link" href="posts/upworthy-ab-testing/index.html">What Makes a Headline Work? →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 238</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Bayesian Statistics</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Bayesian inference including prior elicitation, conjugate analysis, and hierarchical modeling. MCMC methods (Gibbs sampling, Metropolis-Hastings), modern computational techniques (HMC, variational inference), and applications to complex models.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Python</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">MCMC</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Hierarchical Models</span>
    </div>
    <a class="rpc-course-link" href="posts/bayesian-optimization/index.html">Bayesian Optimization from Scratch →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">CS 289A</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Introduction to Machine Learning</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Theoretical foundations and applications of ML from problem formulation to deployment. Unsupervised learning (k-means, PCA), regression and classification, deep learning architectures (CNNs, RNNs, transformers), and generative models. Includes PyTorch implementation and backpropagation.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Python</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">ML Theory</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Deep Learning</span>
    </div>
    <a class="rpc-course-link" href="posts/cs289-ranking/index.html">When Does Ranking Help? →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 254</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Modern Statistical Prediction and Machine Learning</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Probabilistic machine learning theory covering empirical risk minimization, complexity bounds, and uniform laws. Model evaluation via cross-validation, regularization schemes, classification with proxy losses, and connections between linear models and more sophisticated methods.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Statistical Learning Theory</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Regularization</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Cross-Validation</span>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>

<h2 class="rpc-term-heading">Fall 2025</h2>

<div class="rpc-course-grid">

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 243</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Statistical Computing</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Statistical computing and data science in Python. UNIX and bash scripting, version control, data manipulation, text processing, object-oriented programming, parallel processing, databases and big data, computer arithmetic, simulation and Monte Carlo methods, numerical linear algebra, and optimization.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Python</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">UNIX / Bash</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Parallel Computing</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Numerical Methods</span>
    </div>
    <a class="rpc-course-link" href="posts/genetic-algorithm/index.html">Evolutionary Feature Selection →</a>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 201A</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Advanced Probability</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Measure-theoretic probability, convergence concepts, laws of large numbers, central limit theorems, and the foundational theory underpinning statistical inference.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Measure Theory</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Convergence</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Probability Theory</span>
    </div>
  </div>

  <div class="rpc-course">
    <div class="rpc-course-code">STAT 201B</div>
    <div class="rpc-course-name">Advanced Statistics</div>
    <p class="rpc-course-desc">Statistical inference theory including sufficiency, exponential families, hypothesis testing, asymptotic theory, and the foundations of decision theory.</p>
    <div class="rpc-skill-pills">
      <span class="rpc-pill">Inference</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Asymptotics</span>
      <span class="rpc-pill">Decision Theory</span>
    </div>
  </div>

</div>
```
